key_risks.description: Asia Pacific price/mix dilution. Q2 price/mix was (9)% and six-month price/mix (8)%, driven by unfavorable mix and affordability initiatives. Six-month segment operating income fell to $1,192 million from $1,271 million, and the six-month margin fell to 40.9% from 45.6% even with 11% concentrate volume growth. Volume is not yet converting into profit.

Operating cash flow quality. Management cites a benefit from the trade accounts receivable factoring program (the amount is not quantified), lower income tax payments and lower annual incentive payments as drivers of the increase in operating cash flow. These may not repeat, and the six-month comparison base of $(1,391) million is distorted by a $(9,231) million working-capital swing.

Foreign-currency dependence of profit growth. About 5 points of the 9% Q2 operating income increase came from favorable currency, so underlying operating income growth of roughly 4% trails organic revenue growth. A stronger dollar would reverse this tailwind, and a stronger dollar against the rupee, yen, peso and lira already offsets part of it.
Higher commodity costs partly offset gross margin gains. Management also cites increased marketing spending, partly timing-related, which could pressure margins if it does not normalize.

Operational and cybersecurity risk at fairlife. The company disclosed a ransomware event at its fairlife U.S. operations that temporarily suspended production. A majority of production has resumed, and the company believes the incident has not had, and is not reasonably likely to have, a material impact.
key_risks.source_citation: MD&A — Structural Changes, Acquired Brands and Newly Licensed Brands

key_risks.description: Trademark impairment signal. The company recorded a decrease in the fair value of a trademark because of revised projections, including a slower projected long-term category growth rate, an intensifying competitive environment and more focused innovation and international rollout plans. This raises the risk of further impairments in slower-growing categories.

Unresolved U.S. tax dispute over transfer pricing. A 2020 Tax Court ruling largely upheld IRS adjustments, leaving about $2.7 billion in additional taxes (roughly $6 billion with interest), and the company is appealing. The appeal is still live, so cash taxes or a reserve change could materially affect cash flow.

Supplier finance exposure. Obligations confirmed as valid under the supplier finance program were $1,431 million, up from $1,363 million at year-end. This stretches payables through a bank-intermediated program and could add hidden leverage if banks tighten terms.

Lumpy concentrate shipments versus unit case volume. Management expects full-year concentrate sales volume growth to be slightly behind unit case volume growth, so reported revenue growth could lag consumer demand in coming quarters.

bull_case: Q2 growth was broad-based: net operating revenues rose 7% to $13,380 million, with concentrate volume +4%, price/mix +2% and FX +2%, partly offset by (1)% from divestitures. Volume and pricing both contribute, so growth does not depend on a single lever.
Operating income rose 9% to $4,672 million. Gross profit margin expanded to 62.9% from 62.4% on pricing, FX and the Nigeria finished-product divestiture. Diluted EPS rose to $1.03 from $0.88.

Unit case volume accelerated, with Asia Pacific concentrate volume up 11% and India and Southwest Asia up 13% on a six-month basis. Energy drinks are growing across regions, and North America Trademark Coca-Cola grew 5% over six months.

Six-month operating cash flow was $7,543 million vs $(1,391) million a year ago. After $684 million of capex, this covered $4,562 million of dividends and $663 million of buybacks, with roughly $6.9 billion of implied free cash flow.

The balance sheet is deleveraging: long-term debt fell to $37,001 million from $42,119 million, and interest expense fell to $369 million from $445 million in Q2. The company also has $6.6 billion of unused backup credit lines.
Full-year guidance was raised to approximately 5% organic revenue growth (from 4% to 5%), and comparable EPS growth to 9-10% (from 8-9%), signaling management confidence going into the Q3 print.
Latin America (+16% revenue) and North America (+8%) show pricing power that offsets Asia Pacific mix dilution, and Asia Pacific Q2 operating income still edged up to $656 million.
bear_case: Asia Pacific price/mix of (9)% offsets nearly all of 11% concentrate volume growth, leaving segment revenue up only 1%. Six-month operating income fell to $1,192 million from $1,271 million and the margin fell to 40.9% from 45.6%. Volume is not clearly converting into profit.

About 5 points of the 9% Q2 operating income growth came from favorable FX, implying roughly 4% underlying growth, below 6% organic revenue growth. Reported margin expansion to 34.9% from 34.1% may reflect translation more than operating leverage.

Operating cash flow was boosted by receivables factoring (unquantified), lower tax payments and lower incentive payments. Dividend and buyback coverage of about 1.3x on six-month free cash flow is therefore not a clean run rate. A prior-year dividend base of $2,283 million also looks inconsistent with the current $4,562 million.
Management expects full-year concentrate sales to be slightly behind unit case volume, so reported revenue could lag consumer demand. Concentrate shipment timing has swung results between quarters.

The IRS transfer-pricing appeal is unresolved (about $2.7 billion of additional tax, roughly $6 billion with interest, and as much as $20 billion in a worst case per press reports). A reversal would materially hit cash and capital returns.

A trademark fair value decline tied to slower category growth, flat North America water, sports, coffee and tea volume, and the fairlife ransomware production suspension show weakness in growth adjacencies and operational resilience.

Supplier finance obligations rose to $1,431 million from $1,363 million, and commodity costs and marketing spending are headwinds to margin expansion. Shares trading near 52-week highs after the print leave less room for a miss.

what_to_watch.text:
**Asia Pacific Price/Mix vs. Volume:** Asia Pacific concentrate volume rose 11% in Q2, but price/mix was (9)% on unfavorable mix and affordability initiatives, so segment revenue grew only 1%. Six-month segment operating income fell to $1,192 million from $1,271 million, and the six-month margin dropped to 40.9% from 45.6%, which suggests growth is being bought with lower revenue per case. That said, Q2 operating income edged up to $656 million from $647 million and the Q2 margin was essentially flat at 44.1% vs 44.2%, so the drag looks concentrated in Q1 and part of it reflects geographic mix as India and Southwest Asia (+13% volume) outgrow the rest of the segment.

-> Monitor Asia Pacific price/mix, operating margin versus the roughly 41-44% range, and any management split between like-for-like pricing and geographic or channel mix.

**Quality of Operating Cash Flow and Capital Returns:** Six-month operating cash flow of $7,543 million less $684 million of capex implies about $6.9 billion of free cash flow, covering $4,562 million of dividends and $663 million of buybacks by roughly 1.3x. However, management credits receivables factoring (unquantified), lower tax payments and lower incentive payments for the increase, and the prior-year dividend of $2,283 million looks inconsistent with a roughly $4.5 billion half-year run rate, so the comparison base needs verification. Factoring costs were $27 million vs $36 million, but the volume of receivables sold is not disclosed.

-> Monitor Q3 operating cash flow, any quantification of factoring and working-capital benefits, and management commentary on dividend and buyback priorities.

**Volume and Price/Mix Balance, and Concentrate vs. Unit Case Timing:** The 10-Q shows Q2 consolidated volume +4% (concentrate), unit case volume +5%, price/mix +2% and FX +2%. Management has described a more balanced 2026 growth algorithm, with volume and price/mix contributing relatively equally, and the 10-Q guides full-year concentrate growth slightly behind unit cases. On the other hand, the Q2 press-release summary cites different unit case and price/mix figures, so the 10-Q should be treated as the anchor until the basis difference is reconciled. Q2's volume acceleration also follows a 3% unit case gain in Q1, so durability is unproven.

-> Monitor Q3 unit case volume, concentrate-to-unit-case gap and consolidated price/mix for evidence that organic growth stays in the mid-single digits.

**Operating Leverage and FX Contribution:** Q2 operating income rose 9% to $4,672 million, and the operating margin rose to about 34.9% from 34.1%, helped by lower operating expenses, lower other operating charges and pricing. However, roughly 5 points of that growth came from favorable currency, implying underlying growth of about 4% against 6% organic revenue growth, partly because marketing spending and commodity costs rose. Marketing was partly timing-related, so underlying leverage is probably neutral to modestly positive rather than clearly negative.

-> Monitor Q3 operating income growth ex-FX, the marketing spending cadence and the currency headwind or tailwind embedded in updated full-year comparable EPS guidance.

**Raised Full-Year Outlook and the Q3 Print:** The updated outlook calls for approximately 5% organic revenue growth (from 4% to 5%) and comparable EPS growth of 9-10% including a currency tailwind of about 3% and a roughly 1% acquisitions and divestitures headwind. Q2 comparable EPS of $0.97 beat the $0.93 consensus and revenue was $13.38 billion, which sets a high bar after a 6% share price jump. On the other hand, the filing guides concentrate sales slightly behind unit case volume for the full year, and the implied second-half organic growth depends on volume holding up against tougher pricing comparisons.

-> Monitor whether Q3 organic revenue growth of about 5% is delivered with both volume and price/mix positive, and whether full-year guidance is raised again.

**IRS Transfer-Pricing Appeal:** A 2020 Tax Court ruling largely upheld IRS adjustments, leaving about $2.7 billion in additional taxes (roughly $6 billion with interest), and the company is appealing, with press reports putting as much as $20 billion at stake. Six-month income taxes were $1,682 million vs $1,715 million, and management cites lower income tax payments as a contributor to operating cash flow, so any adverse resolution would reverse that benefit. That said, the reserve and the contingency disclosure were not verified here and the sources are news and video commentary.

-> Monitor contingency disclosures, any change in the unrecognized tax benefit reserve, and management commentary on the appeal timeline and cash tax outlook.

**Balance Sheet Flexibility and Debt Paydown:** Long-term debt fell to $37,001 million from $42,119 million, Q2 interest expense fell to $369 million from $445 million, and the company had $6.6 billion of unused backup credit lines with only $9 million of new debt issued in the half. However, total current liabilities rose to $25,200 million from $21,281 million, supplier finance obligations rose to $1,431 million from $1,363 million, and the retrieved text includes no maturity schedule, so near-term refinancing needs are not verified.

-> Monitor current maturities of long-term debt, supplier finance balances and any new issuance announced alongside Q3 results.

**Growth Adjacencies: Emerging Markets, Energy and fairlife:** Volume is broadening beyond sparkling drinks, with Asia Pacific up 8% for six months across categories, energy growing across regions, and secondary sources describing fairlife retail sales above $4 billion after the roughly $6.2 billion milestone investment. However, North America water, sports, coffee and tea volume was flat, a trademark was written down on a slower category growth outlook, and a ransomware event temporarily suspended fairlife production, though management says it is not reasonably likely to be material.

-> Monitor fairlife production status and disclosed segment contribution, further impairment indicators, and volume trends in water, sports, coffee and tea and energy.
